analysis: Both changed files are test-only. EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift has a one-line change at ~L312: the helper's `case .toolCall:` becomes `case .toolCall, .toolCallDelta:`. The change is only to accommodate a new enum case in MLXServerGenerationEvent. The helper skips those events, so no test assertion is weakened that affects a security control. The visible head units (L1221-2472) cover heartbeat grant re-slicing, request routing, forced tool_choice fail-closed validation, forged schema metadata rejection, cacheSalt plumbing (the tenant scope is passed as the per-request salt, relevant to T-041), cancellation propagation, runtime guards and KV-backend fallback heartbeat clamping. These are unchanged; I saw no weakened assertions, no secrets and no production behavior changes. GemmaOpenRouterLiveTests.swift now reassembles streamed tool-call fragments by wire index instead of appending raw deltas. It is a live-test helper and does not cross a trust boundary, touch keys, attestation or the coordinator wire. The production-side `.toolCallDelta` streaming event, which presumably emits tool-call fragments for `auto`, is not in the supplied batch. A next pass should check that the production code validates and bounds tool-call fragments, in particular that forced tool_choice (required/named) still never exposes unvalidated text and that fragments are encrypted like other SSE chunks (T-008). That is outside the evidence supplied here, so it is recorded as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
